claims.text: What it measures Usually the spine and one or both hips are scanned with high- and low-energy X-rays to measure bone mineral density
claims.quote: In a DXA scan, the target areas, typically the spine and one or both hips, are imaged using x-rays of high and low energy (hence the term "dual energy").

claims.text: If spine or hip can't be used (for example hardware from a hip replacement or spinal fusion), the distal radius is scanned
claims.quote: If the spine or a hip is unsuitable for accurate assessment by DXA (eg, because of hardware from prior total hip arthroplasty or spinal fusion surgery), the distal radius can be scanned

claims.text: Pitfall: significant osteoarthritis at the scanned site may raise the reported density
claims.quote: The presence of significant osteoarthritis in the target areas may increase the reported bone density.

claims.text: Reading the report T-score: standard deviations from the peak bone mass of a healthy young person of the same sex and race/ethnicity
claims.quote: The T-score corresponds to the number of standard deviations that the patient's bone mineral density differs from the peak bone mass of a healthy, young person of the same sex and race/ethnicity.

claims.text: A T-score of -2.5 or lower defines osteoporosis
Z-score: compared with people of the same age and sex; used for children, premenopausal women, or men
claims.quote: The Z-score corresponds to the number of standard deviations that the patient's bone mineral density differs from that of a person of the same age and sex and should be used for children, premenopausal women, or men

claims.text: A fragility fracture diagnoses osteoporosis whatever the bone density score
claims.quote: Alternatively, osteoporosis can also be diagnosed based on the occurrence of a fragility fracture, regardless of the bone mineral density score.
